title: Inject a clock into a rate limiter
problem: SlidingWindowLimiter reads time.monotonic() directly, so testing 'blocked until the window passes' would mean really waiting. limiter.py already defines a Clock protocol and a SystemClock. Write FakeClock (a clock that only moves when told to) and refactor the limiter to take any Clock, defaulting to the real one. The limiting rule itself must not change.
requirements: FakeClock(start=0.0): now() returns the current fake time, which only changes through advance(seconds)
advance with a negative number raises ValueError and leaves the time unchanged; advance(0) is allowed
FakeClock satisfies the Clock protocol structurally: it must NOT inherit from Clock
SlidingWindowLimiter(limit, window, clock=None) stores the clock it uses as self.clock; with no clock it uses a new SystemClock()
allow() gets the time only from self.clock.now()
Keep the rule: a call allowed at time t counts against the limit until t + window (exclusive)
contract: FakeClock(start: float = 0.0); now(self) -> float; advance(self, seconds: float) -> None.  SlidingWindowLimiter(limit: int, window: float, clock: Clock | None = None); attribute clock; allow(self) -> bool
expectedBehavior: clock = FakeClock(); lim = SlidingWindowLimiter(1, 10.0, clock=clock); lim.allow() is True; lim.allow() is False; clock.advance(10); lim.allow() is True
edgeCases: A call exactly window seconds after an allowed call is allowed again (the old one has expired)
advance(0) is fine; advance(-1) raises and doesn't move the clock
Two limiters sharing one clock still count separately
No clock passed: the limiter works with the real clock
hints: Conceptual: this is the Go pattern 'depend on an interface, pass the real implementation in production and a fake in tests'. FakeClock just needs a now method; it never mentions Clock. The limiter should ask its clock for the time instead of the time module.

Specific: FakeClock keeps the current time in an attribute set in __init__. The limiter's __init__ gets a clock parameter with default None, and picks SystemClock() when it's None. Why not write clock: Clock = SystemClock() as the default? (PY.M02.L04.)

Implementation: in FakeClock, now returns self._now; advance checks seconds < 0 first (raise ValueError), then does self._now += seconds. In the limiter: self.clock = clock if clock is not None else SystemClock(), and in allow replace time.monotonic() with self.clock.now().
evaluation: allow() no longer calls the time module
The default clock is created per limiter (no object built once in the signature)
